target_audience: High school AP Calculus or introductory university students

sections.title: The Wall: Explicit vs. Implicit
lecture_lines: Meet explicit functions, where y is clearly isolated.
But what if y is trapped inside the equation?
We call these "implicit" equations, like a locked box.
Consider this circular force field: x² plus y² equals 25.
Finding the slope here requires a new mathematical tool.
animations: Show an explicit function y = x^2 in white (#FFFFFF) at the top of the screen.
Display the implicit equation x^2 + y^2 = 25 in cyan (#00FFFF) below the explicit one.
Animate a red (#FF0000) 'Locked Box' appearing around the 'y' variable in the implicit equation.
Draw a circle of radius 2.5 in cyan (#00FFFF) with a moving dot representing a drone.
Add a yellow (#FFFF00) tangent line at the drone's position to show its instantaneous slope.

sections.title: The Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Reminder
lecture_lines: Remember the Chain Rule: it's our engine for differentiation.
Treat y as a hidden function nested inside x.
Every y-derivative must leave a dy/dx tail behind.
animations: Show the expression (y)^3 in white (#FFFFFF) inside a light green (#90EE90) container.
Transform (y)^3 into 3y^2 in white (#FFFFFF) while the container fades.
Attach the term (dy/dx) in orange (#FFA500) next to 3y^2 as the 'chain rule tail'.

sections.title: The Strategy: The Four-Step Recipe
lecture_lines: First, differentiate both sides of the equation normally.
Attach a dy/dx whenever you differentiate a y term.
Next, group all terms containing dy/dx on one side.
Factor out dy/dx to isolate it from the rest.
Finally, solve for dy/dx to find the derivative.
animations: Display the equation d/dx(x^2) + d/dx(y^2) = d/dx(25) in white (#FFFFFF).
Show the derivative 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, with dy/dx highlighted in orange (#FFA500).
Move the 2x term to the right side to get 2y(dy/dx) = -2x.
Divide both sides by 2y to isolate the dy/dx term.
Highlight the final solution dy/dx = -x/y in yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Guided Practice: The Laser Tangent
lecture_lines: At point (3, 4), our derivative is negative three-fourths.
This value represents the exact slope of the tangent.
See the laser beam tilt perfectly against the circle.
animations: Draw a circle in cyan (#00FFFF) and mark the point (3, 4) with a red (#FF0000) dot.
Show the substitution 2(3) + 2(4)(dy/dx) = 0 in white (#FFFFFF) next to the graph.
Animate the calculation steps to simplify the equation to 8(dy/dx) = -6.
Display the final slope value dy/dx = -3/4 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Draw a yellow (#FFFF00) tangent line (laser beam) at (3, 4) with the calculated slope.

sections.title: Application: The Rollercoaster of Curves
lecture_lines: Some curves, like this infinity loop, are impossible to isolate.
Implicit differentiation is our superpower for these complex paths.
Meet Turbo the Snail racing along this intricate track.
We calculate his exact direction at any given coordinate.
This math keeps Turbo on track throughout the loop.
animations: Display the equation (x^2 + y^2)^2 = x^2 - y^2 in purple (#BF40BF) at the center.
Animate a white (#FFFFFF) dot named 'Turbo' tracing the figure-eight path of the lemniscate.
Show a green (#00FF00) tangent vector at Turbo's position, rotating to show the changing slope.
